newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon CFO-'96 net income down, EPS up.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon CFO-'96 net income down, EPS up.

text.p: Raytheon Co chief financial officer Peter D'Angelo Friday said he expected the Lexington, Mass-based company's 1996 earnings per share to top last year's $3.25 EPS, but declined to say by how much.
Earlier in the day at least one analyst, Paul Nesbit of JSA Research Inc, lowered his EPS on Raytheon to $3.60 from $3.65.

Raytheon announced earlier it expected a 15 percent drop in net operating income for the year. "This year we expect to report about $274 million in operating income," D'Angelo said in a conference call with reporters.

"When you look at that reduction in operating income is associated with E&C and appliances, year-to-year," D'Angelo, who noted that the third quarter of 1983 was the last time Raytheon had a decline in operating income without a special charge.

Chuck Miller, who heads Rathyeon Engineering & Constructor division, which with over $3 billion of revenues projected for 1996 is the largest single unit within the company, said financing troubles in India, Indonesia and China had contributed to delays in getting projects going.
"We don't book these projects until we get the financing in place," Miller said, adding Raytheon had been under contract for Invicta in Indonesia for more than year.

The Vyzag project in India, also a power project, "is partially booked, but we're waiting for the second package to be booked," Miller said, adding that he hoped to have that happen in the fourth quarter, along with another project in China.
As the gross domestic products of countries gain the need for power "is still out there," he said, "There will eventually be a catchup period, particularly in industries like power."
